issues.legal_issue: The civil-court bar for matters assigned to a rent controller does not apply to a subtenant’s suit asserting a tenancy arising after the principal tenancy ended before the later rent-control law, where the dispute is not assigned to the controller.
material_facts: The landlord obtained an ejectment decree against the principal tenant before the later rent-control law came into force.
The subtenant was not a party to the ejectment suit, and the decree did not determine the subtenant’s interest.
The subtenant claimed that the principal tenancy’s termination had made the subtenant a tenant directly under the landlord.
The subtenant brought a civil suit seeking protection against the landlord taking possession.
The earlier rent-control law provided that, upon eviction of the principal tenant, the subtenant would be deemed a tenant of the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The civil-court bar did not prevent the suit. The subtenant could seek a declaration of the asserted tenancy in a civil court.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17(2) and 17(3) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, the Controller decides specified disputes about lawful subletting, including disputes arising during the subsistence of the principal tenancy in the circumstances covered by those provisions. Section 18(1) concerns a subtenant whose principal tenancy is ended by an eviction order under the 1958 Act. Section 18(2), by contrast, deems a lawful subtenant to become a tenant where the principal tenant’s interest was determined before the 1958 Act commenced but the subtenant’s interest continued. No provision assigned a dispute about that section 18(2) status to the Controller; section 50 therefore did not bar a civil suit about it. Independently, section 20 of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952, had conferred a vested tenancy right on the subtenant upon eviction of the principal tenant, and the 1958 Act did not remove that right or confer jurisdiction on the Controller to determine it. Mohd. Mahmood v. Tikam Das was distinguished: it held that a civil suit was barred when filed during the period in which the Controller could decide the dispute, while leaving open the question of civil-court jurisdiction after that period. The Court also noted support in the Punjab High Court decision in Smt. Viran Wati Devi v. Jaswant Rai.

rule.if: civil_suit_seeks_recognition_of_subtenant_tenancy and ((main_tenancy_ended_before_later_rent_law and lawful_subtenancy_survived_that_ending and later_rent_law_assigns_no_controller_process_for_that_legacy_dispute) or (earlier_rent_law_conferred_direct_tenancy_on_subtenant and later_rent_law_did_not_remove_that_right and later_rent_law_assigns_no_controller_process_for_that_right))

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_recognition_of_subtenan: A subtenant brought a civil suit seeking recognition or protection of a claimed tenancy under the landlord.
predicates.main_tenancy_ended_before_later_rent_law: The principal tenant’s interest ended before the later rent-control law came into force.
predicates.lawful_subtenancy_survived_that_ending: The subtenancy was lawful and the subtenant’s interest was not ended when the principal tenancy ended.
predicates.later_rent_law_assigns_no_controller_pro: The later rent-control law provides no procedure for the rent controller to decide a dispute about the surviving subtenant’s claimed status arising from the earlier termination.
predicates.earlier_rent_law_conferred_direct_tenanc: An earlier rent-control law made the subtenant a direct tenant of the landlord upon eviction of the principal tenant.
predicates.later_rent_law_did_not_remove_that_right: The later rent-control law did not take away the tenancy right conferred on the subtenant by the earlier law.

issues.definition: When a subtenant seeks recognition of a tenancy in a civil suit and either the surviving subtenancy stems from the principal tenancy ending before the later rent-control law, or an earlier law had already conferred a direct tenancy that the later law left intact, the civil suit is maintainable if the later law assigns no such dispute to the rent controller.
